point_of_use_paragraphs: [F5] Choice scope ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-metric-compactness]]): $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used once, in step 3.1, through the sequential-closure direction of [F4]; the compactness statements of clauses 3 and 4 use $\mathrm{AC}_\omega+\mathrm{DC}$, and only through the published compactness of $X_2$ and the general fact that continuous images of compact spaces are compact.

statement:
Fix $a\ge100$ and put

$$R:=\sqrt a+3,\qquad l:=\sqrt a-3\ge7,\qquad S:=[-R-1,R+1]^2,\qquad S(x,y):=(y,x).$$

Let $C=C(a,R)$ be the constant of [[lem-perturbed-scalar-recurrence-root-bounds]], let $0<\varepsilon\le1/6$ with $\eta:=C\varepsilon\le1$, and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be open with $S\subseteq U$. Let $G=(A,B):U\to\mathbb R^2$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto its image whose components satisfy, on $S$,

$$|A(x,y)-y|\le\varepsilon,\quad |\partial_xA(x,y)|\le\varepsilon,\quad |\partial_yA(x,y)-1|\le\varepsilon,$$

$$|B(x,y)-(y^2-a-x)|\le\varepsilon,\quad |\partial_xB(x,y)+1|\le\varepsilon,\quad |\partial_yB(x,y)-2y|\le\varepsilon,$$

and assume in addition that $H:=S\circ G^{-1}\circ S$ is defined and of class $C^2$ on a neighbourhood of $S$ and satisfies the same six inequalities on $S$ with the same constant $\varepsilon$. For each sign $u$ let $M_u$ be the root map of [[lem-perturbed-scalar-recurrence-root-bounds]] applied to $G$, let $V$ be the inverse branch of [[lem-close-map-first-component-has-uniform-inverse]], and let $M^H_u,V^H$ be the corresponding objects for $H$. Then:

1. **(coding)** for every $s\in X_\pm$ there is exactly one $q(s)\in B_R$ with $q_n(s)=M_{s_n}\bigl(q_{n-1}(s),q_{n+1}(s)\bigr)$ for all $n\in\mathbb Z$; it satisfies $l\le|q_n(s)|\le R$, $\operatorname{sign}q_n(s)=s_n$ and $R-|q_n(s)|\ge\tfrac34$, $|q_n(s)|-l\ge\tfrac34$; setting $v_n(s):=V(q_n(s),q_{n+1}(s))$ and

$$z_n(s):=\bigl(q_n(s),v_n(s)\bigr),\qquad h_G(s):=z_0(s)=\bigl(q_0(s),V(q_0(s),q_1(s))\bigr),$$

one has $G(z_n(s))=z_{n+1}(s)$ for all $n$;
2. **(conjugacy and chaos)** $h_G$ is a continuous bijection of $(X_\pm,D_\pm)$ onto $\Lambda_G:=h_G(X_\pm)$; granting the Axiom of Countable Choice (used once, through the equivalence between closed and sequentially closed subsets of $\mathbb R^2$), it is a homeomorphism, and $G\circ h_G=h_G\circ S_\pm$, so $\Lambda_G$ is $G$-invariant; $\Lambda_G$ is sequentially compact, and compact under the Axioms of Countable and Dependent Choice; and $G|_{\Lambda_G}$ is continuous, topologically mixing, has dense periodic points, and is sensitive with sensitivity constant $2l$; hence $G|_{\Lambda_G}$ is chaotic in the stated sense;
3. **(fixed points)** for each sign $u$ the constant code $\bar u$ gives a fixed point $z_{\bar u}:=h_G(\bar u)=\bigl(\rho_u,V(\rho_u,\rho_u)\bigr)$, where $\rho_u=M_u(\rho_u,\rho_u)$ is the unique element of $u\,[l,R]$ with $\rho_u=M_u(\rho_u,\rho_u)$; these two fixed points are hyperbolic;
4. **(transverse homoclinic points)** let $s\in X_\pm$ be nonconstant with $s_n=u$ for $|n|\ge N$. Then $z_*:=h_G(s)\ne z_{\bar u}$, and there are $C^1$ curves $\gamma_s,\gamma_u:(-\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_0)\to\mathbb R^2$ with $\gamma_s(0)=\gamma_u(0)=z_*$, $\gamma_s\bigl((-\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_0)\bigr)\subseteq W^s(z_{\bar u})$, $\gamma_u\bigl((-\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_0)\bigr)\subseteq W^u(z_{\bar u})$, tangent vectors $\gamma_s'(0)\in C^s_{3/4}$, $\gamma_u'(0)\in C^u_{3/4}$; since $C^s_{3/4}\cap C^u_{3/4}=\{0\}$ the tangent lines are distinct, so $z_*$ is a transverse homoclinic point of $z_{\bar u}$ ([[def-stable-unstable-cones-and-line-slopes]]).
point_of_use_paragraphs: [F6] Topological vocabulary and sequential closure ([[def-cm-topologically-mixing-dense-periodic-and-sensitive-maps]], [[def-dense-top]], [[def-metric-continuity]], [[def-metric-topology]], [[thm-metric-sequential-closure]], [[lem-metric-limits-unique]], [[def-metric-compactness-variants]], [[def-metric-compactness]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]): the definitions of mixing, dense periodic points, sensitivity, continuity, open and closed sets, and fixed points; closed subsets of a metric space are exactly the sets containing all limits of their convergent sequences, limits in metric spaces are unique, the implication "closed $\Rightarrow$ sequentially closed" is choice-free, and the converse implication uses the Axiom of Countable Choice once.

Grant the Axioms of Countable and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]), inherited from the compactness and homeomorphism clauses of [[thm-explicit-perturbed-horseshoe-and-transversality]]. Fix $a\ge100$, let $w$, $\beta_\delta$, $P=\pi/2+\delta$ and the stroboscopic map $G_\delta$ be as in [[def-smooth-periodic-oscillator-pulse-model]], and let $X_\pm$, $S_\pm$, $D_\pm$ be the two-sign shift space of [[def-bilateral-symbol-and-bounded-sequence-space]]. Then there is $\delta_0>0$, depending only on $a$ and $w$, such that for every $0<\delta<\delta_0$:

[F3] Under the Axioms of Countable and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]), the perturbed horseshoe ([[thm-explicit-perturbed-horseshoe-and-transversality]]): for every $\varepsilon\le1/6$ with $C\varepsilon\le1$ and every $C^2$ diffeomorphism $G$ onto its image on a neighbourhood of $S$ satisfying the six closeness inequalities with constant $\varepsilon$ on $S$, and whose conjugate $S_w\circ G^{-1}\circ S_w$ does the same, the conclusions of clauses 1-4 above hold for $G$ under these same axioms with sensitivity constant $2(\sqrt a-3)$ and with all codes constant outside finite sets.

[F4] The dyadic time set $D=\{kT/2^n: n\in\mathbb N,\ 0\le k\le 2^n\}$ is countable and dense in $[0,T]$: it is the union over $n$ of the finite sets $D_n=\{kT/2^n: 0\le k\le2^n\}$ ([[thm-countable-union-of-countable]], [[def-countable]]), and for $t\in[0,T]$ and $\delta>0$ one has $|t-kT/2^n|\le T/2^n<\delta$ for $n$ large and $k:=\lfloor 2^nt/T\rfloor$ ([[cor-archimedean-reciprocal]], [[lem-integer-part]]).

statement:
Assume the Axioms of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]).
Use the spaces of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]] and the
absolutely continuous representatives supplied by
[[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]].

(a) *Bounded intervals.* Let $0<L<\infty$ and $u,v\in H^1(0,L)$. Then
$\int_0^Lu\,\overline{v'}=u^*(L)\overline{v^*(L)}-u^*(0)\overline{v^*(0)}
-\int_0^Lu'\,\overline v .$

(b) *Endpoint-vanishing space.* $H^1_0(0,L)=\{u\in H^1(0,L):u^*(0)=u^*(L)=0\}$,
with the traces $u^*(0),u^*(L)$ of the continuous representative.

(c) *Second-order identity.* For $u,v\in H^2(0,L)$,
$\int_0^L\bigl(u''\overline v-u\,\overline{v''}\bigr)
=\bigl[u'^*\overline{v^*}-u^*\overline{v'^*}\bigr]_0^L,$
where the bracket denotes
$u'^*(L)\overline{v^*(L)}-u^*(L)\overline{v'^*(L)}
-u'^*(0)\overline{v^*(0)}+u^*(0)\overline{v'^*(0)}$.

(d) *Half-line and line.* If $u,v\in H^1(0,\infty)$, then
$\int_0^\infty u\overline{v'}=-\int_0^\infty u'\overline v$, both integrals
being absolutely convergent. The same identity holds for
$u,v\in H^1(\mathbb R)$ with $\int_{\mathbb R}$ in place of
$\int_0^\infty$.

statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on an
infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $H$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-dimension]]), let $c\in\mathbb R$ lie in the
resolvent set of $A$, and assume that the resolvent
$R_c:=(A-c)^{-1}\in\mathcal B(H)$ is compact
([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-compact-linear-operator]]). Then:

(a) $H$ has a complete orthonormal family $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of
eigenvectors of $A$; writing $\mu_n$ for the eigenvalue of $e_n$, one has
$|\mu_n|\to\infty$ (each eigenvalue repeated according to its finite
multiplicity), and every eigenspace of $A$ is finite dimensional;

(b) $\sigma(A)$ consists exactly of the eigenvalues $\mu_n$ of $A$ and has no
other points, and the essential spectrum is empty:
$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)=\varnothing$
([[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]]); thus
every spectral point of $A$ is an isolated eigenvalue of finite
multiplicity;

(c) for every $z$ in the resolvent set of $A$ the resolvent $(A-z)^{-1}$ is
compact.
point_of_use_paragraphs:
1.1 [Spectral decomposition of $R_c$] The resolvent $R_c$ is self-adjoint (it is the inverse of the self-adjoint operator $A-c$, hence commutes with the resolvent of $A$ and equals its own adjoint by [F1]) and compact by hypothesis. It is injective: if $R_cx=0$, then $x=(A-c)R_cx=0$ by [F1]. By [F2], with $\ker R_c=\{0\}$, the nonzero eigenspaces of $R_c$ are finite dimensional with real nonzero eigenvalues, and the union of orthonormal bases of those eigenspaces is a complete orthonormal family $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ of eigenvectors of $R_c$ with eigenvalues $
u_i
e0$. The eigenvalue set is countable, being the union over $k\ge1$ of the finite sets $\{
u:|
u|\ge1/k\}$ ([[thm-countable-union-of-countable]], [[def-countable]]), so $I$, a union of finitely many bases over a countable set of eigenvalues, is finite or countably infinite; it is infinite because a finite complete orthonormal family would be a finite spanning set of $H$ (its span is finite dimensional, hence closed, and equals its closed span, [[cor-finite-dimensional-subspaces-are-closed]]), so that $H$ would have a finite basis and be finite dimensional ([[cor-every-spanning-set-contains-a-basis]], [[def-linear-basis]], [[def-dimension]]), contrary to hypothesis. Hence $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ can be indexed as $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$, and then $
u_n	o0$: for every $\varepsilon>0$ only finitely many indices $n$ satisfy $|
u_n|\ge\varepsilon$ by [F2]. [F1, F2]

statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the Axiom of Dependent Choice and the
Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a parameter $\alpha>0$, define the transverse
subspace
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for a.e. }k\Bigr\}$$
with the $L^2$ inner product, define the bounded multiplier-valued function
$\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$ and $\Pi(0):=0$, and let
$M_\Pi$ be multiplication by $\Pi$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Write
$\varepsilon(k):=\alpha|k|$ and let $M_\varepsilon$ be multiplication by
$\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}:=M_\varepsilon|_{\mathfrak h}$.
Let $F(\mathfrak h)$ be the Fock space of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] with sectors
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and for $n\ge1$ define
$$T_n\psi:=\varepsilon_n\psi,\quad \varepsilon_n(k_1,\dots,k_n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha|k_i|,\qquad D(T_n):=\{\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}:\varepsilon_n\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\},$$
and $T_0:=0$ on $\mathbb C$. Finally put
$$H_f:=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_n,\qquad D(H_f):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(\mathfrak h):\ \sum_n\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$
Then:

(a) $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ is a closed separable subspace of
$L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$, invariant under $M_\varepsilon$, and
$\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on
$\mathfrak h$ with $D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\varepsilon f\in\mathfrak h\}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]],
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]);

(b) each $T_n$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with the displayed domain
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]);

(c) $H_f$ is self-adjoint and positive with domain $D(H_f)$; it commutes with
every sector projection $\Pi_n$ (i.e. $T_n$ maps its sector into itself);

(d) for every $\beta>0$ the bounded operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]) is not compact and in particular not trace
class ([[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]); more
precisely its restriction to the one-particle sector equals the multiplication
operator $M_{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}$ on $\mathfrak h$, which is not compact, and
the restriction of a compact operator to a closed invariant subspace is compact.

The identification of $\mathfrak h$, $\varepsilon$ and $H_f$ with physical
transverse photons in a chosen frame is a separate model assumption and is not
asserted here; no thermal interpretation of $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is claimed either.

statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral and
Bochner suppliers. Fix $\hbar>0$, let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $K$ and $A$ be self-adjoint operators on $H$ with
spectral projection-valued measures $E_K$ and $E_A$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), let $W\in\mathcal B(H)$ be unitary
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), and put
$$U_K(t):=e^{-itK/\hbar},\qquad U_A(s):=e^{-isA/\hbar}\qquad(s,t\in\mathbb R)$$
in the spectral calculus of [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], which are
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). Write
$\Phi_K(g)=\int g\,dE_K$ for bounded Borel $g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$
([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]), and let
$K_W:=WKW^{*}$ with $D(K_W):=WD(K)$. Then:

(a) $K_W$ is self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure
$$E_{K_W}(B)=WE_K(B)W^{*}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
its flow satisfies $e^{-itK_W/\hbar}=WU_K(t)W^{*}$ for every $t$, and the
conjugated family $s\mapsto WU_A(s)W^{*}$ is a strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group whose infinitesimal generator is
$-\frac{i}{\hbar}WAW^{*}$ with domain $WD(A)$
([[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]);

(b) the following are equivalent:

  (i) $U_A(s)U_K(t)=U_K(t)U_A(s)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$;

  (ii) $E_A(B)E_K(C)=E_K(C)E_A(B)$ for all Borel sets $B,C\subseteq\mathbb R$;

  (iii) $U_K(t)D(A)=D(A)$ and $U_K(t)AU_K(t)^{*}=A$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$;

(c) if a bounded $B\in\mathcal B(H)$ satisfies $BU_K(t)=U_K(t)B$ for every
$t\in\mathbb R$, then $B\Phi_K(g)=\Phi_K(g)B$ for every bounded Borel
$g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$; in particular $BE_K(C)=E_K(C)B$ for every Borel
$C\subseteq\mathbb R$;

(d) if (i)-(iii) of (b) hold, then $E_A(B)U_K(t)=U_K(t)E_A(B)$ for every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$.

statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for a declared isolated
system with state space $H$, assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$
and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]); use the symmetry vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]. Assume the
Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Dependent
Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable of the
system with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and put
$W(s):=e^{-isA/\hbar}$. Then the following are equivalent:

(i) $W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$;

(ii) $E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)$ for all Borel sets $B,C\subseteq\mathbb R$;

(iii) $U(t)D(A)=D(A)$ and $U(t)AU(t)^{*}=A$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$.

When they hold:

(a) **Conserved law.** The outcome law of $(A,u_A)$ is time-independent: for
every preparation $\rho$, every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\psi(0)}(B)\ \text{for a unit }\psi\ \text{with }\psi(t)=U(t)\psi(0).$$

(b) **Conserved moments.** If $\psi\in D(A)$ is a unit vector, then the mean and
the second moment of the law of $A$ in the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ are
finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero values
$\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; if a moment is infinite at
$t=0$, no equality of finite quantities is claimed.

(c) **Unitary symmetries of the dynamics.** If a unitary operator $S$ is a
symmetry in the sense of clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]], that is
$S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and
$S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S$, then $S\,U(t)=U(t)\,S$ for every $t$;
if in addition $S$ is self-adjoint, then the outcome law of the assigned sharp
observable $(S,u_S)$ with its spectral coordinate unit is time-independent in
every preparation.

(d) **Status and exclusions.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2 and P4
and the cited mathematics. Its symmetry hypothesis is the strong commutation of
the flows or, equivalently, of the spectral measures, not a formal commutator
identity on a small domain; no definite value of a conserved observable is
asserted; no converse from the constancy of laws to the commutation conditions
is claimed for unbounded $A$; and no concrete model potential, apparatus,
measurement record or empirical result is introduced.

Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space with
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]),
let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable, and let
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1}),\qquad V_{a}(x):=V(x-a),$$
be the model's bounded-potential energy operator with $M_{V}$ multiplication by
$V$ and $T_{a}:=T_{a}^{(2s+1)}$ the componentwise translations
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c), [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]]). Then:

(a) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$:
$$T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}},$$
and $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b)
if and only if $V_{a}=V$ almost everywhere;

(b) if $T_{a}$ is a symmetry for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$, then $V$ is almost
everywhere constant; in that case $H_{V}=H_{0}+cI$ on $W^{2,2}$ for
$H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ and $c$ the constant, and the translations
form a strongly continuous unitary group of symmetries;

(c) **Momentum conservation for translation-invariant models.** Let $V$ be
almost everywhere constant and let $c$ be that constant. Then for every
$k\in\{1,2,3\}$ the momentum component $P_{k}$ is a conserved observable of the
model with energy $H_{V}$: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(0)}(B);$$
if $\psi(0)\in D(P_{k})$ is a unit vector, the mean and second moment of the
law of $P_{k}$ are conserved with time-zero values $\langle P_{k}\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $\|P_{k}\psi\|^{2}$; and the coordinate translations satisfy
$T_{te_{k}}=e^{-itP_{k}/\hbar}$ for all $t$, so the generators of the
one-parameter symmetry groups are the momentum components;

(d) **Scope.** The statement concerns the componentwise massive model with real
bounded measurable potentials. It asserts no momentum conservation for a
potential that is not translation invariant — the translation-covariance
theorem transports the position law and conjugates the dynamics, but does not
by itself conserve momentum — and it makes no claim about singular, unbounded,
periodic, boundary or relativistic models, no discrete symmetry group, no
apparatus and no empirical result.

([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$r=2s+1$, be the model's state space with componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$,
let $U(R)$ be the spatial rotation action and $\Pi$ the spatial parity action
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]]), let $U_{i}(t)=U(R_{i}(t))$ be the
coordinate rotation subgroups with Stone generators $L_{i}$ on the Schwartz
classes ([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]]), let
$V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable, and let
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),\qquad V_{R}(x):=V(R^{-1}x),\quad V_{P}(x):=V(-x),$$
be the model's bounded-potential energy operator with flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{V}/\hbar)$ in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b)
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c) applied componentwise,
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a)).
Then:

(a) for every $R\in SO(3)$ one has $U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V_{R}}$, and $U(R)$
is a symmetry of $H_{V}$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b)

(b) if $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere for every $R\in SO(3)$, then every $U(R)$
is a symmetry, the map $R\mapsto U(R)$ is a strongly continuous unitary
symmetry group of the declared dynamics, and each generator $L_{i}$ is a
conserved observable of the model with energy $H_{V}$ in the unit
$\mathrm{J\,s}$ of the model's action
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]): for every preparation $\rho$,
every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
and for a unit vector $\psi(0)\in D(L_{i})$ the mean and second moment of the
law of $L_{i}$ are finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero values
$\langle L_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}$;

(c) if $V(-x)=V(x)$ for almost every $x$, then $\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V}$ on
$W^{2,2}$, so $\Pi$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$, and $\Pi$ is a symmetry if and
only if $V_{P}=V$ almost everywhere; moreover, reading the self-adjoint
unitary $\Pi$ as an assigned sharp observable with its spectral coordinate in
the dimensionless unit of its eigenvalues $\pm1$, the outcome law of $\Pi$ is
time-independent in every preparation:
$$\mu^{\Pi}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{\Pi}_{\rho(0)}(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},\ t\in\mathbb R);$$

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the
cited mathematics, and it concerns the componentwise massive model with real
bounded measurable potentials. Rotations and parity act on the spatial factor
only: no SU(2) lift, no rotation of the internal factor and no spin angular
momentum are introduced. The rotational and parity invariance hypotheses are
exactly the displayed almost-everywhere identities; no concrete potential,
apparatus, measured spectrum or empirical result is asserted, and no
characterization of the invariant potentials beyond these identities is
claimed.

statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the causal-curve class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Chart independence.** Local absolute continuity in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (a) is independent of the
chosen chart and of the smooth atlas: if one chart representative of a curve
is absolutely continuous on every compact parameter subinterval, then so is
every other one.

**(b) Velocity and smooth composition.** At every interior parameter value
$t$ at which one chart representative is differentiable, every chart
representative is differentiable, the velocity $\gamma'(t)$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (b) is well defined and
independent of the chart, and the set of parameter values at which some
chart representative is differentiable has full measure in the domain. For
every smooth map $F$ of an open subset of $M$ into $M$ whose domain contains
the image of $\gamma$, the composite $F\circ\gamma$ is locally absolutely
continuous and $(F\circ\gamma)'(t)=dF_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t))$ at almost
every parameter value $t$.

**(c) Piecewise $C^1$ curves.** Every piecewise $C^1$ curve (in the
one-sided-tangent convention of
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) is locally absolutely
continuous; a piecewise $C^1$ curve all of whose tangents are future causal
is a future causal curve, and if in addition its tangents are future
timelike, it is a future timelike curve.

**(d) Concatenation.** If $\gamma_1:[a,b]\to M$ and $\gamma_2:[b,c]\to M$ are
future causal curves (respectively future timelike curves) with
$\gamma_1(b)=\gamma_2(b)$, then the concatenation $\gamma:[a,c]\to M$,
$\gamma(t):=\gamma_1(t)$ for $t\le b$ and $\gamma(t):=\gamma_2(t)$ for
$t\ge b$, is a future causal (respectively future timelike) curve; the same
holds for any finite chain of such curves.

**(e) Reparametrization.** If $\varphi:J\to I$ is a strictly increasing
$C^1$ diffeomorphism of intervals with $\varphi'>0$ and $\gamma:I\to M$ is
locally absolutely continuous, then $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is locally
absolutely continuous and $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is future causal (respectively
future timelike) exactly when $\gamma$ is. Moreover $\gamma$ is
future-inextendible if and only if $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is
future-inextendible, and this equivalence holds for every strictly increasing
continuous surjection $\varphi$ of intervals, not only the $C^1$ ones.

**(f) Relations.** The relation $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is reflexive and transitive, and
$p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$ for all $p,q$; the relations $J^{\pm}$ and
$I^{\pm}$ of that definition are therefore nested, $I^{\pm}(S)\subseteq
J^{\pm}(S)$ for every $S\subseteq M$.

statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $u$ be a temporal function
on it in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]
clause (e), and write $\nabla u$ for its gradient. Then:

**(a)** $du(v)=g(\nabla u,v)>0$ for every nonzero future causal vector $v$.

**(b)** For every future causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ in the class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], the composite $u\circ\gamma$ is
locally absolutely continuous, its derivative satisfies
$(u\circ\gamma)'(t)>0$ at almost every $t\in I$, and consequently
$$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))\qquad\text{whenever }a<b\text{ and }\gamma \text{ is not constant on }[a,b].$$

**(c)** $u$ is a time function on $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (d); every level
set $u^{-1}(c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, is achronal; and $(M,g,N)$ is causal and
chronological: it admits no nonconstant future causal curve with equal
endpoints.

statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,\eta,N)$ be the
flat model of [[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]], with its
global inertial chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, written $x=(x^0,z)$ with
$z\in\mathbb R^3$ (clauses (a), (b) and (e) of that definition), and let
$\gamma:I\to M$ be a future causal curve in the class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** $x^0\circ\gamma:I\to\mathbb R$ is strictly increasing.

**(b)** For all $a<b$ in $I$,
$$\bigl|z(\gamma(b))-z(\gamma(a))\bigr|\le x^0(\gamma(b))-x^0(\gamma(a)),$$
and consequently $\gamma$ is injective and its image is a $1$-Lipschitz graph
over the interval $(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)$.

**(c)** If $\gamma$ is future-inextendible then
$\sup\,(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)=+\infty$; if $\gamma$ is past-inextendible then
$\inf\,(x^0\circ\gamma)(I)=-\infty$. Hence if $\gamma$ is inextendible then
$x^0\circ\gamma$ is a strictly increasing surjection onto $\mathbb R$, and
for every $c\in\mathbb R$ the parameter set
$\{t\in I:x^0(\gamma(t))=c\}$ is a singleton.

**(d)** The coordinate function $u:=x^0$ is a temporal function of the flat
model in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]
clause (e): its gradient is the vector field $\nabla u=-\partial_0$ on all of
$M$, with $\eta(\nabla u,\nabla u)=-1<0$ and $du(\partial_0)=1>0$
everywhere.
